newsitem.title: DUBAI: Emirates uplifted tonnage up 23pct over past year.
newsitem.headline: Emirates uplifted tonnage up 23pct over past year.

text.p: Emirates Airline's air freight division, Emirates Sky Cargo, said on Monday it registered a 23 percent increase in tonnage uplifted in the year to end-March 1997 over the previous year.

It uplifted a total of 160,257 tonnes during the year April 1, 1996 to March 31, 1997, despite slack world trade and an increase in cargo capacity during the first half of that period, Emirates said in a statement.

"The capacity increase was due mainly to passenger aircraft newly-converted to cargo freighters hitting the cargo market at the same time that the growth in world trade -- and therefore demand for capacity -- slackened," it said.
"The highly-populated Pacific Rim region in particular was plagued by falling yields, in some markets by as much as 32 percent."

Ram Menen, Emirates senior general manager for cargo, said despite the problems, Emirates managed "the situation by taking a positive approach and building up business by the conversion of certain commodities from ocean traffic to air."

He said a market pickup in the second half of the year strengthened demand and pushed yields almost back to their original level, though profitability in general for most carriers continued to be eroded by high fuel costs.
"At Emirates, we are bullish about growth in the next three to four years, with world trade expected to be stronger than ever, particularly in consumer commodities," Menen said.
He said all players involved in the logistics chain in the cargo industry needed to be more "pro-active and change accordingly to enhance distribution requirements".
